ApiProvider.description:
A provider that speaks a standard API: Lighthouse knows the format of the
requests, and the project says where to send them.

baseUrl.description: Where requests go. Default: the spec's own service.

extraBody.description:
A JSON object merged shallowly into every request body, its keys
overriding the body's own (the OpenAI SDK's `extra_body`).

keyEnv.description:
The environment variable that holds the API key; none for a service
that needs no key. Default: the spec's own.

logprobs.description:
Read the answer from the probability of the first token (`yes` or
`no`) instead of asking for a number; OpenAI's `logprobs` parameter.
Only for a model whose first token is the answer. Default: false.

spec.description:
The API: `openai` (Chat Completions, which OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM
and LM Studio also speak) or `typesafe` (System One). Others will join.

Evaluation.description:
How a rule's check is judged by `lighthouse eval`. A policy, not a
meaning: changing it moves no meaning version.

precision.description: The precision a check must reach, from 0 to 1. Default: 0.9.

recall.description: The recall a check must reach, from 0 to 1; no target when absent.

Formatter.description:
The command that formats a file of a language, by the command contract of
fixes: exit `0` succeeds, stdout carries only the result, stderr is for
people.

env.description: Extra environment variables; the rest is cleared to an allowlist.

FormatterSpec.description:
How a formatter is written: `[gofmt, -w]` is the short form (scratch copy,
path appended).

GeneratedSpec.description: What a project says about generated code.

check.description:
`skip`: no decision checks generated code; `include`: every decision
does. Unset, each decision's own scope says. A rule's `generated`
setting wins over both.

files.description: Globs of project-relative paths that are generated code.

Level.description:
A level a project can set: a severity, or `off`, which only
configuration has.

Metadata.description:
Who a resource is. Identity is `name`; grouping is by label, never by
where the document is stored.

annotations.description: Free notes; never used to select.

uid.description:
Identity that outlives the name: a UUID v4 assigned once, never derived
from the name (Kubernetes `metadata.uid`). Renaming a resource keeps it.

ModelInput.description: What a `command` model is given on stdin.

oneOf.description: The request as JSON, as a model plugin gets it.
The request as text for a language model, with the answer's shape.

ModelOutput.description: How a `command` model prints its answer.

ModelProvider.description:
A provider of models, named under `[models.providers.<name>]`: a provider,
as a check or a fix is. A model is named `<provider>/<model>`.

oneOf.description:
A plugin process that offers models. The `options` say how to reach
them (`spec`, `baseUrl`, `keyEnv`, `logprobs`, `extraBody` for `model-http`); the model part of
the reference goes with every request.

cost.description: What one answer costs, when the plugin's own figure is not right.

plugin.description: A listed plugin that offers models.

oneOf.description:
Any program that reads a request and prints an answer, under the
process contract: no shell, its own process group, a time limit, a cap
on output, an environment cleared to `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `LANG`,
`TMPDIR`, the declared `env` and the variable `keyEnv` names, and the project's
trust. An answer that does not fit the task's shape is an abstention.

argv.description:
The program and its arguments; `{model}` stands for the model part
of the reference.

env.description: Variables the program is given besides the allowlist.

keyEnv.description:
The variable of the user's environment that holds the program's
key; it is passed through, and no other secret is.

pointer.description:
RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the answer inside the printed JSON, when
the program wraps it in an envelope.

timeout.description: How long one run may take, such as `90s`. Default: 120s.

ModelsSpec.description:
The `models` table of a project: its bindings and limits, and its own
providers.

budget.description:
Requests a run may send to models that cost something; the subjects
of the rest are left to review. Default: 200.

classification.description:
The model (`<provider>/<model>`), or the route of several, that judges
a decision no rule binds and no trained model is attached to. A request
moves to the next model of a route when one fails. When the route
abstains, the subject is left to agent review.

explore.description:
The share, from 0 to 1, of the subjects an attached model fails that are
sent on to the next layer as if it had abstained, so that labels keep
coming from where the model is surest. The same subjects every run.
Default: 0.05.

providers.description:
The providers the project defines, by name; a name that is built in
overrides it.

routing.description: Which model of a route a request starts at. Default: `ordered`.

Names.description:
One name or several, in the order written: the standard APIs a provider
speaks (each operation uses the one that covers it: classification
`typesafe`, else `openai`), or the models of a route.

Output.description: Where a command that fixes or formats a file leaves the new text.

oneOf.description:
In the scratch copy of the file, which is appended to `argv` (or fills
an `{file}` argument).
On stdout, which carries only the text.

OverrideSpec.description: Rules for the files and languages that match.

files.description: Globs of project-relative paths; empty matches every path.

languages.description: Language ids; empty matches every language.

PluginEntry.description: A plugin in `plugins`: a bare id, or an id with where to find it.

PluginRefSpec.description:
A listed plugin. `path` (relative to the config directory) names the
plugin directory instead of searching the plugin locations; `timeout` is
the per-request limit for process plugins, such as `30s`.

constructorPrefixes.description:
The name prefixes that make a function a constructor in this
language, replacing what its provider declares. Every decision that
tells a constructor apart shares them.

formatter.description: The command that formats a file of the language after a fix.

ProjectSpec.description:
A project's configuration, and the shape of a shareable one: `extends`
names any project, the way an ESLint config extends a shareable config.
An extended project contributes its `extends`, `rules` and `overrides`.
Its `plugins` and `languages` belong to the project that is run.

extends.description:
Projects whose rules apply first, in order: the `recommended` and
`strict` projects of each pack (`core/recommended`), or any `Project`
document of the catalog.

generated.description:
Which files are generated code, beyond what the providers and
`.gitattributes` say, and whether it is checked.

languages.description:
Options per language id; `formatter` is the host's, the rest goes to
the language's provider.

models.description: The models that judge the decisions rules cannot prove.

overrides.description: Rules that apply to some files or languages only, after `rules`.

plugins.description:
Plugins that provide rules and languages; a bare id searches the
plugin locations.

rules.description: Level and options per decision id.

ProviderSpec.description: A provider as the project writes it.

Routing.description: Which model of a route a request goes to first.

oneOf.description: The first model, then the others in the order written.

Each request starts at the next model, so load is spread; the others
follow in the order written, wrapping.

evaluation.description: How `lighthouse eval` judges this rule's check.

generated.description:
Check generated code with this rule (`true`) or not (`false`),
whatever the decision's scope and the project's `generated.check` say.

model.description:
The model, or the route of several, that judges this decision, before
the project's `models.classification`. When it abstains, the subject is
left to agent review.

options.description: The decision's options, as its own schema declares them.

RuleSetting.description:
How a rule is written in a spec: `warn`, `off`, or
`{ level: warn, options: { max: 10 } }`.

Stdin.description: What a command that checks, fixes or formats a file is given on stdin.
